description: Trigger evals for autonomous-readiness: it fires when a defined project needs a go or no-go check before an unattended overnight run, while approve-plan, autonomous-run, autonomous-board and problem-framing handle plan approval, driving the run, viewing a live run, and shaping a fuzzy objective.

should_trigger: is this project set up well enough to leave running overnight?
I want to hand the inventory-sync project to an unattended run tonight. The charter, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md and the plan are all written. Tell me whether anything is missing before I walk away.
Before I go to bed and let the agent grind through the whole plan, check that the project definition is complete and give me a yes or no with every gap listed.
The mobile app has a login flow and a camera screen declared as runtime surfaces, but I never set up any way to capture evidence from a device. Would a night run just stall on those?
go/no-go for tonight's unattended run on the billing-export task?

should_not_trigger.prompt: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md looks final to me. Lock it as the approved baseline and stamp TASK_STATE.md so slices can start.
The plan is approved and the readiness check already came back clean. Start the supervised session and work through the waves now.
The overnight run has been going for three hours. Show me a board of what is done, in progress and escalated so far.
I only have a vague idea that we should make onboarding better. No task exists yet. Help me figure out if that is even the right problem.
The requirements are clear and decisions are locked, but there is no plan yet. Break the work into small reviewable slices with exit criteria.
